Letter of Invitation
Development Partnership Administration-II, Ministry of External Affairs, New Delhi invites
sealed proposal on two covers system from the eligible bidders for imparting training to foreign
participants under its Indian Technical an Economic Cooperation (ITEC) programme, as per the
specifications given in this tender.
Interested bidders may submit their bids as per the  Request  for  Proposal  (RfP) document
available  on  MEA  website  http://www.mea.gov.in and  Central  Procurement  Portal
http://eprocure.gov.in. Important dates pertaining to this tender are as below:

 A Pre bid meeting for queries and clarifications on the RfP document will be held on appointed
date at Room No. 2079, 'B' Wing, Ministry of External Affairs, Jawaharlal Nehru Bhawan (JNB),
New Delhi. Technical bids shall be opened on the appointed date and time. After scrutiny of Technical

The Ministry of External Affairs reserves the right to accept or reject any / all bids without

amendments, etc. shall be posted on MEA  website  http://www.mea.gov.in and Central Public
Procurement Portal Website: http://eprocure.gov.in/eprocure/app.

SECTION I:
 INSTRUCTIONS TO BIDDERS (ITB)
1. Invitation for offers
1.1. Development Partnership Administration-II, Ministry of External Affairs, New Delhi invites
sealed proposals on two covers system from the eligible bidders for imparting training to
foreign participants under its Indian Technical an Economic Cooperatiion (ITEC) programme,
as per the specifications given in this tender.
1.2. The successful bidder(s) are expected to design and deliver short term training programmes
with the course duration ranging from as short as one week to upto 12 weeks. Each course can
typically have 30 participants. Each training programme needs to be dynamically customised,
in consultation with MEA, to meet the specific requirement of MEA. MEA reserves the right
to modify the areas of training, numbers of offered training programme/s by any of the
selected bidder and/or number of participants therein.
1.3. This selection shall be for three years and can be further extended by one year at each instance
upon mutual agreement.
1.4. The cost of preparing the proposals are not reimbursable and MEA reserves the right to reject
any proposal without assigning any reason.
1.5. The Institutes must observe highest standards of ethics during the selection process and later
during the execution of the work.  MEA may reject a proposal at any stage if it is found that
the Institute(s) selected has indulged in corrupt or fraudulent activities in competing for or in
executing the assigned work in question and may also declare the Institute(s) ineligible or
blacklist it either indefinitely or for a stated period of time.
2.Contact information:
Section Officer (ITEC-I)
Development Partnership Administration-II

3. Eligibility Criteria
3.1.The Bidder should have been successfully short-listed in the process of Invitation of Expression
of Interest conducted by MEA vide EOI No. DPA-II/551/05/2016, dated 29 May 2018 and
should have been specifically invited to participate in the RfP.  
4. Cost and Availability of RfP Document
4.1.The RfP document can be downloaded from MEA’s website ( www.mea.gov.in) or CPP portal
(http://eprocure.gov.in/eprocure/app).  However, the processing fee (non-refundable) against
the document has to be paid by the applicant in the form of DD/Pay Order  for Rs.2000/-
favouring “Pay and Accounts Officer, Ministry of External Affairs, New Delhi”.
4.2.The original instrument in respect of Processing Fee must be submitted to Section Officer (ITEC),
Room No. 2079, Jawaharlal Nehru Bhawan (JNB), New Delhi on or before proposal

submission date/time as mentioned in critical date sheet, failing which the proposal shall not
be considered.
5. Timelines:
Date of Publishing 20.12.2018 (1000 Hrs)
RfP Document Download/ Sale Start Date 20.12.2018 (1000 Hrs)
Online Queries Start Date 20.12.2018 (1000 Hrs)
Online Queries End Date 01.01.2019 (1500 Hrs)

6. Pre Proposal meeting for queries on the RfP Document
6.1.A pre-proposal meting for  queries and clarifications on this document will be held at Room
No.2079 ‘B’ Wing, Jawaharlal Nehru Bhawan, 23-D, Janpath, New Delhi as per schedule
provided in clause pertaining to important dates.  All prospective applicants / authorized
representative of the applicants who have downloaded the document may attend the meeting to
get  their  queries  and  clarification  replied,  if  any.   The  applicants  should  depute
representative(s) of appropriate level who should be well conversant with the subject and
proposal requirements.  Due to security reasons, Bidders, willing to attend the meeting, are
requested to convey their contact details to MEA latest by  1500 hrs on 01.01.2019 ,before the
meeting, so that necessary arrangements could be made.  Details are to be conveyed through
email to soitec1@mea.gov.in.  The queries/suggestions should be submitted only on CPP
Portal on or before online clarification Date/time as mentioned in critical date sheet.  The
answer to the queries will be provided only on CPP Portal after the Meeting.  The queries
received after due date/time or through e-Mail/letter will not be considered.
7. Amendment of RfP  Documents
7.1. At any time prior to the last date for submission of proposals MEA may, for any reason-
whether at its own initiative or in response to a clarification requested by a prospective bidder,
modify the terms of this document by an amendment.  Applicants are advised to keep referring
the CPP Portal for any corrigendum/change.  There wouldn’t be any newspaper advertisement
towards the same.
8. Period of validity of bids
8.1. Proposal shall be valid for a minimum 180 days from the date of opening of proposal. A bid
valid for a shorter period shall stand rejected.

8.2. In exceptional circumstances, MEA may request the consent of the bidder for an extension to
the period of bid validity.   The request and the response thereto shall be made in writing.  The
bid security provided under clause 9 of Section 1  shall be suitably extended. The bidder may
refuse the request without forfeiting this bid security. A bidder accepting the request and
granting extension will not be permitted to modify his bids.
9. Bid Security/Earnest Money Deposit (EMD) 
9.1. Bids must be accompanied by a bid security of Rs. 2,00,000/- (Rupees Two Lakh only) only in
the form of Bank Guarantee (BG) drawn on any nationalized,  scheduled bank payable at
Delhi in favour of “Pay and Accounts Officer, Ministry of External Affairs, New Delhi”
payable at New Delhi, valid upto 45 days beyond the validity of the offer   i.e. 225 days from
the date of bid opening.
9.2. Proforma of Bank Guarantee for Bid Security is enclosed as Annexure – III.
9.3. The bid security of unsuccessful bidders shall be returned after finalisation of the selection
process.  Bid security shall be forfeited if a bidder withdraws from the RfP process after
opening of technical bids.  No interest will be payable on the EMD/Bid Security amount.
9.4. Bid Security of successful bidder shall be returned after submission of Performance Band
Guarantee (Clause 17).  In case, the selected bidder fails to furnish the Performance Bank
Guarantee in due time or fails to furnish the acceptance in writing in due time, his EMD would
be forfeited.
9.5. Original instrument in respect of EMD must be submitted to Section Officer (ITEC), Room
No.2079, Jawaharlal Nehru  Bhawan (JNB), New Delhi, on or before bid submission date /
time as mentioned in critical date sheet, failing which the bid shall not be considered.
10. Preparation of Proposals
10.1. Interested Institutes are required to submit their proposal in two covers i.e. Technical and
Financial proposal as specified below:
10.2. Envelope No. 1 “Technical Proposal’:  The following documents are to be uploaded online in
the given format, with proper seal and signature of authorized persons on each uploaded page.

10.3. In preparing the Technical Proposal, applicants are expected to take into account the
requirement and conditions outlined in this document and to provide exact information for all
the parameters required for evaluation of the Technical Proposals.
10.4. Envelope No.2 “Financial Proposal”: Price schedule should be submitted online only in the
form of  BOQBasicIT.xls.  The prices should be mentioned in figures as well as words
wherever mentioned in the BOQ BasicIT.xls.  The bidder should carefully cross check the
prices entered in figures with corresponding figures converted in words.
11. Submission of Proposal
11.1. All documents, as per requirement shall be uploaded  online through Central Public
Procurement Portal Website:  http://eprocure.gov.in/eprocure/app and further no documents
will be accepted offline prospective bidders are accordingly advised to go through instructions
provided at Central Public Procurement Portal.
11.2. The bidder is expected to examine all instructions, forms, terms and specifications in the RfP
documents.  Failure to furnish all information required as per the RfP document or submission
of the bids not substantively responsive to the RfP document in every respect will be at
bidder’s risk and may result in rejection of the bid.
11.3. Both technical and financial bid are to be submitted concurrently duly digitally signed on the
Central Public Procurement Portal.  The bidders shall have a valid digital signature certificate
for participation in the online tender.  The cost of digital signatures, if any, will be borne by
respective tenderer.
11.4. These shall not contain any terms and conditions, printed or otherwise, which are not
applicable to the Bid.  The conditional bid will be summarily rejected.  Insertions, postscripts,
additions and alterations shall not be recognized, unless confirmed by bidder’s signature.
11.5. The original hard copies of EMD of Rs. 2,00,000/- (Rs. Two Lakh  only) in the form of a Bank
Guarantee in the prescribed format or Demand Draft / Pay Order in favour of “Pay & Account
Officer, Ministry of External Affairs, New Delhi” and of Processing Fee of Rs. 2,000/- (Rs.
Two Thousand Only) in the form of Demand Draft / Pay Order in favour of “Pay & Account
Officer, Ministry of External Affairs, New Delhi” are required to be submitted in a sealed
envelope superscribed as “EMD and Processing Fee  in connection with RfP for Selection of
Training Institutes for imparting short-terms training to foreign participants under ITEC
Programme – Basic IT.” at Section Officer (ITEC), Room No.2079  Jawaharlal Nehru Bhawan
(JNB), New Delhi, on or before bid submission date/time as mentioned in critical date sheet,
failing which the bid shall not be considered.
12. Authorized Signatory
12.1. The person signing the bid should be the duly authorized representative of the bidder and
whose signature should be verified and certificate of authority should be scanned and
submitted.  The power or authorisation or any other document consisting of adequate proof of
the ability of the signatory to bind with the firm/ company should be scanned and annexed to

the bid.  All certificates and documents (including any clarifications sought and any
subsequent correspondences) received hereby, shall, as far as possible, be furnished and signed
by the Authorized Representative.
13. Opening and Initial determination of compliance with RfP requirements
13.1. Online Technical Proposals (complete in all respect) received alongwith Bid Security and
Processing  Fee in physical form by stipulated time will be opened, as per timelines indicated
in the tender document and in the presence of bidders or their  authorized representatives who
chose to attend, at the office of Section Officer (ITEC), Room No. 2079, Jawaharlal Nehru
Bhawan (JNB), New Delhi – 110011.
13.2. Bid received without Bid Security and Processing Fee in physical forms will be rejected
straight away.
13.3. All the Technical proposals that are submitted on time will, in the first instance be examined to
ascertain fulfillment of eligibility criteria and submission of required documents in support
thereof. MEA may choose to discontinue the evaluation of any proposal which it considers
unacceptable prima facie for any reason such as; The proposal is not a reasonable effort to
respond to the requirements of the RFP; or is vague or lacking in material particulars/
information sought or is not accompanied with relevant documents or the Processing
fee/EMD.
13.4. MEA may waive any minor infirmity or non-conformity or irregularity in a bid which doesn’t
constitute a material deviation, provided such waiver doesn’t prejudice or affect the relative
ranking of any bidder.
14. Selection Process
14.1. Bidders who have submitted all required documents in their Technical Proposal, if required,
may be invited to make presentations on their Technical Proposal on a date/time to be
specified  and conveyed by the MEA.   MEA may seek clarifications from the bidders and the
bidders are expected to respond/provide the information /clarifications within the stipulated
time.  The failure to provide the information may lead to disqualification of the bidder.
14.2. The Technical Proposals will be evaluated on the basis of the following criteria and a

14.3. Only the Bidders scoring 50 or more marks for the above “Preliminary Technical Score (Pt S)”
would  be  considered  for  further  evaluation.  MEA representatives  will  be  visiting
campus/facilities of the bidders, scoring 50 or more marks in PtS, to assess the infrastructure,
inspect the premises, meet the faculty members, etc. and to verify the claims made by the
bidder.  Any wrong or misleading information will lead to disqualification and other penal
actions, including the forfeiture of EMD.  Based upon the assessment of this visit, the
institutes will be given a relative “Visit Score (VS)” out of total 100 marks.
14.4. A “Tecnical Score (TS) of each bidder would then be calculated as follows:
TS =  ( 0.7 x PtS )  + ( 0.3 x VS )

14.5. MEA will open price proposal only of those bidders who scored 50% or more marks in the
“Preliminary Technical Score ( Pt  S)” , in the presence of those bidder or their authorized
representative who choose to attend the financial bid opening, at the time and date, to be
informed later.
14.6. Envelope No.2 "Financial Bid”: Price schedule should be submitted online only in the form of
BOQ.xls. The prices should be mentioned in figures as well as in words wherever mentioned
in the BOQ.xls. The bidder should carefully cross check the prices entered in figures with
corresponding figures converted in words. 
15.  Evaluation Criteria and Identification of Best Evaluated Bid
15.1. Evaluation Criteria to be adopted will be Quality cum Cost Based System (QCBS) where
“Technical Score (TS)”  will get a weightage of 70%, and Financial Bid Score a weightage of
30%.
15.2. Description of variables used: 
 TS is the technical score for each bid.
 TShigh   is the Technical score achieved by the Bid that was scored best among all
responsive bids
  C is the Commercial Bid Price quoted by the bidder,  on per week per participant basis.
 P= (Rates quoted for line-item 1 of
BoQ + Rates quoted for Line item 2 of
BoQ*7)
  CL is the value of lowest of all evaluated bid price among all responsive bids.
 Final Score (FS) for each Bid shall be computed as follows:
FS = (70 *  TS / TShigh )  + (30 *CL//C)
15.3. The Bids, will be arranged in descending order of respective Final Score (FS) value for
consideration of selection and award of work.
15.4. From the time the Technical Proposal are opened to the time the contract is awarded, if any
Applicant wishes to contact MEA on any matter related to its proposal, he/she should do so
only in writing.  Any effort by the applicant to influence the process of proposal evaluation or
contract award decisions may result in summary rejection of the proposal of the Institute.
16. Award of Work
16.1. The successful bidder(s) are required to design and deliver the short term training programmes
for maximum  upto t he allotted number of “man-weeks”  (i.e. sum of total allotted slots in a
course X duration of the course in weeks)  of training per year for the period of their selction.
The participants actually attending the course may vary. 
16.2. Each training programme needs to be dynamically customised, in consultation with MEA, to
meet the specific requirement of MEA, which may be different than what are being submitted
with this RfP. MEA reserves the right to modify the areas of training, numbers of offered
training programme/s by any of the selected bidder and/or number of participants therein.
16.3. A Letter of Acceptance cum Supply Order in accordance to the terms and conditions of this
RfP document shall be issued by the MEA.  This selection shall be for three years and can be
further extended by one year at each instance upon mutual agreement. A separate supply order
will be issued for each financial year.
17. Performance Bank Guarantee (PBG)

17.1. Within 30 working days of Supply Order the successful Bidder shall furnish to the Purchaser a
Performance bank guarantee for an amount equivalent t o Rs Thirty Six Lakh only  as per the
format provided at Annexure II.  This Performance Bank Guarantee shall remain valid till six
months later than the end of a given  financial year. The validity of Performance Bank
Guarantee would needs to be extended annually during the period of selection.
17.2. The Performance Security will be discharged by the Purchaser after completion of the
Suppliers’ performance obligations including warranty obligations (if any) under the contract.
18. Purchaser’s Right to amend the Scope of Work
18.1. If, for any unforeseen reasons, purchaser is required to change the Scope of Supply, this
change shall be acceptable to the bidder without change in the unit  price quoted.
18.2. Purchaser reserves the right to reject one/ all the bids or cancel the tender without assigning
any reasons there for.
19. Corrupt or Fraudulent Practices.
19.1. It is expected that the bidders who wish to bid for this project have highest standards of ethics.
MEA will reject bid if it determines that the bidder recommended for award has engaged in
corrupt or fraudulent  practices while competing for this contract.  MEA may declare a vendor
ineligible, either indefinitely or for a stated duration, to be awarded or contact if it at any time
determines that the vendor has engaged in corrupt and fraudulent practices during the
execution of contact.
20. Interpretation of the clauses in the Tender Document/Contract Documents   
20.1. In case of any ambiguity / dispute in the interpretation of any of the clauses in this Tender
Document, MEA’s interpretation of the clauses shall be final and binding on all parties.
END OF SECTION I

SECTION II
GENERAL CONDITIONS OF CONTRACT (GCC)
 
1. Background information of ITEC Programme and Scope of services to be offered by the
selected bidders:
1.1. The ITEC Programme was initiated in 1964, and it is India’s flagship capacity building
programme, offering fully sponsored training courses at premier Indian Institutions to Government
officials and professionals from 161 partner developing countries of different regions of the world
including Asia, Africa, Eastern Europe, Latin America, Caribbean and Pacific island countries.  These
are primarily short-term courses for Government Officers and working professionals  in a wide and
diverse range of skills and disciplines such as finance & accounts, audit, banking, education, planning
& administration, parliamentary studies, crime records, textiles, rural electrification, tool design, IT,
English language etc. In addition, upon specific demand of our partner countries, special customised
courses are also conducted.
1.2. DPA-II Division of the Development Partnership Administration (DPA) in the Ministry of
External Affairs is the nodal division for handling all capacity building programmes under ITEC.  The
ITEC training institutes are fully funded by the Ministry of External Affairs. Applicants themselves can
browse the available courses in different participating institutes under ITEC Programme and can apply
for the suitable programme by filling up the online application form.   To facilitate the application
process for ITEC applicants, an online portal is made available at www.itecgoi.in. The printout of this
application form is submitted to respective Indian Missions, accredited to the applicant's country, duly
forwarded by their nodal/designated Government Department / Agency.  The Indian Missions
recommend the participants through online portal. MEA, consultation with the concerned institute,
finally selects the participants. Upon his final selection, Indian Missions arrange for to-and-fro air
tickets and visas for the participants to attend the programme in India.
1.3. The Institutes are required to receive the selected participants at the airport, provide lodging and
boarding during the training period, impart training, arrange study tour (if included in the course
programme) and upon completion of the programme, see-off the participants at the airport.  Institutes
are required to provide any other emergency support, including medical, for the participants.   Institutes
are to ensure the provisions of continental food at subsidized rates. The payment of food is to be settled
between the participant and the Institute. These all activities are to be done in close coordination with
the Ministry. Institutes are also required to  submit various reports over ITEC online portal as well as
offline. 
1.4. The fee components of ITEC training programme, their current applicable rate and payment
methodology are listed in Section-III.  MEA reserves the right to modify terms at any point of time.
1.5. The successful bidder(s) are required  to design and deliver short term training programmes with
the course duration  ranging from as short as one week to upto 12 weeks. Each course can typically
have 30 participants. The maximum intended number of “man-weeks”  (i.e. sum of total allotted slots in
a course X duration of the course in weeks) of training to be allotted to each Institute in the respective
areas are given in  Section-III. The participants actually attending the course may vary. Each training
programme needs to be dynamically customised, in consultation with MEA, to meet the specific re -
quirement of MEA. MEA reserves the right to modify the areas of training, numbers of offered training
programme/s by any of the selected bidder and/or number of participants therein. This selection shall
be for three years and can be further extended by one year at each instance, upon mutual agreement.

2. Prices
2.1. The ITEC fee structure is provided in Annexure III. While other components are fixed/reimbursed
as per actual, the course fee and the accommodation charges are to be quoted by the bidders. These

(URL: https://eprocure.gov.in/eprocure/app) by clicking on the link “Online bidders Enrollment” on the CPP Portal
which is free of charge.

a password for their accounts.

several parameters. These parameters could include Tender ID, Organization Name, Location, Date, Value, etc.

parameters such as Organization Name, Form of Contract, Location, Date, Other keywords etc. to search for a
tender published on the CPP Portal.

their bids.

documents required to be submitted as part of the bid. Please note the number of covers in which the bid
